title: Coworker bought all my energy drinks
author: Storytime
hook: Every morning, my coworker bought every single can of my favorite energy drink from the office vending machine. I stopped speaking to her. Then she told me why.
story: There's one vending machine on our floor. It has one energy drink I like. A blue can. I used to drink four or five a day. I was working sixty hour weeks. Last month, every morning, the blue cans were gone. Sold out. Every single day. One morning, I came in early and saw my coworker, Linda, feeding dollars into the machine. She bought all eight. I was furious. I asked her why. She just said, I like them. I stopped speaking to her. For three weeks. Last Friday, I had a dizzy spell at my desk. Linda was the first one there. She sat me down, checked my pulse, and called the nurse. Then she pulled open her bottom drawer. It was full of blue cans. Unopened. Dozens. She said, I was an ER nurse for twenty years. Your hands have been shaking since summer. I didn't know how else to help. She'd been leaving bottles of water on my desk every day. I thought it was the cleaners. I saw a doctor yesterday. My heart's okay. Barely. How do I even thank her?
caption: she wasn't stealing my drinks 💙 #storytime
sound: a gentle piano that turns warm and hopeful at very low volume
why: A coworker hoarding your favorite drink is a trending workplace pet peeve, the silent treatment builds tension, the ER nurse twist is moving, and how do I thank her pulls heartfelt comments.

title: My boyfriend said he was a CEO
author: Storytime
hook: My boyfriend told me he's the CEO of his own company. Today at Thanksgiving, his mom told me what the company actually is.
story: I've been dating Marcus for five months. On our first date, he said he was the CEO of a tech company. Always on calls. Always busy at night. Never talked details. I thought it was impressive. Today was my first Thanksgiving with his family. His mom hugged me and said, so you're the girl who finally got him out of his room. I laughed. She didn't. Over pie, I asked her about Marcus's company. She looked at him and said, you mean the gaming team? Marcus is the captain of an online gaming team. Five members. The office is his childhood bedroom. The calls are tournaments. I wanted to disappear. Then his mom kept talking. She said, he won a tournament last spring. Twelve thousand dollars. He paid off my medical bills with it. Every cent. He never told anyone. Marcus turned bright red. He said, I didn't think you'd date a gamer. So I said CEO. Honestly? I don't care about the title. I care that he lied for five months. And also that he paid his mom's medical bills. Should I stay?
caption: CEO of his childhood bedroom 🎮 #storytime
sound: an awkward comedy beat that turns sweet at very low volume
why: Exes and partners who lied about being a CEO are trending, the Thanksgiving mom reveal is funny, the medical bills twist complicates it, and should I stay splits commenters.

title: Our dog ate the whole turkey
author: Storytime
hook: Twenty minutes before Thanksgiving dinner, our dog ate the entire turkey. Then the neighbour we've been feuding with for fifteen years knocked on the door.
story: Every Thanksgiving, my parents host twenty people. Last year, my mom set the turkey on the counter to rest. Twenty minutes before dinner. Our golden retriever, Bruno, got the whole thing. Twenty two pounds. Gone. My mom sat on the kitchen floor and cried. Then someone knocked on the door. It was Mr. Kowalski from next door. My family has been in a feud with him for fifteen years. Over a fence. A tree. A parking spot. My dad hasn't said a word to him since I was ten. Mr. Kowalski was holding a huge roasting pan. A cooked turkey. He said, I saw your dog through the window with a drumstick. My kids cancelled on me. I cooked this for nobody. Take it. My dad stood there for a full minute. Then he said, only if you eat with us. Mr. Kowalski sat at the head of the table. He and my dad talked until midnight. Turns out the whole feud started because my dad thought Mr. Kowalski cut down our tree. It was a storm. This Thanksgiving, he's coming back. And Bruno is banned from the kitchen. Should we make it a tradition?
caption: the dog ended a fifteen year feud 🐶 #storytime
sound: a chaotic comedy beat that turns warm and cozy at very low volume
why: Posted on Thanksgiving day, the dog eating the turkey is a hilarious hook, the feuding neighbour twist is heartwarming, and should we make it a tradition invites happy comments.
